chapters.title: What has come concerning forgetfulness when standing after two rak‘ahs of an obligatory prayer
If one gives the greeting of peace after two or three rak‘ahs and makes two prostrations like those of the prayer or longer
One who does not recite the tashahhud in the two prostrations of forgetfulness
One who pronounces the takbir in the two prostrations of forgetfulness
If one does not know whether one has prayed three or four, one makes two prostrations while seated
Forgetfulness in obligatory and voluntary prayer
If one is spoken to while praying and signals with the hand and listens

arabic_blocks: [1166] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك بن أنس عن ابن شهاب عن عبد الرحمن الأعرج عن عبد الله بن بحينة رضى الله تعالى عنه أنه قال صلى لنا رسول الله ﷺ ركعتين من بعض الصلوات ثم قام فلم يجلس فقام الناس معه فلما قضى صلاته ونظرنا تسليمه كبر قبل التسليم فسجد سجدتين وهو جالس ثم سلم
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-A‘raj, from ‘Abdullah ibn Buhaynah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in two rak‘ahs of one of the prayers. Then he stood up without sitting, and the people stood up with him. When he had completed his prayer and we were waiting for his greeting of peace, he pronounced the takbir before the greeting of peace and made two prostrations while seated. Then he gave the greeting of peace.

arabic_blocks: [1169] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة عن سعد بن إبراهيم عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال صلى بنا النبي ﷺ الظهر أو العصر فسلم، فقال له ذو اليدين الصلاة يا رسول الله أنقصت، فقال النبي ﷺ لأصحابه أحق ما يقول: قالوا نعم فصلى ركعتين أخريين ثم سجد سجدتين قال سعد ورأيت عروة بن الزبير صلى من المغرب ركعتين فسلم وتكلم ثم صلى ما بقى وسجد سجدتين، وقال هكذا فعل النبي ﷺ
english_blocks: Adam related to us. Shu‘bah related to us, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in Dhuhr or ‘Asr and gave the greeting of peace. Dhu al-Yadayn said to him, “The prayer, O Messenger of Allah—has it been shortened?” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions, “Is what he says true?” They said, “Yes.” So he prayed two more rak‘ahs, then made two prostrations.

Sa‘d said: I saw ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr pray two rak‘ahs of Maghrib, give the greeting of peace and speak. Then he prayed what remained and made two prostrations. He said, “This is what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did.”

arabic_blocks: [1170] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك بن أنس عن أيوب بن أبي تميمة السختياني عن محمد بن سيرين عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ انصرف من اثنتين، فقال له ذو اليدين أقصرت الصلاة أم نسيت يا رسول الله، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: أصدق ذو اليدين، فقال الناس نعم فقام رسول الله ﷺ فصلى اثنتين أخريين ثم سلم ثم كبر فسجد مثل سجوده أو أطول ثم رفع
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ended after two rak‘ahs. Dhu al-Yadayn said to him, “Has the prayer been shortened, or did you forget, O Messenger of Allah?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Has Dhu al-Yadayn spoken the truth?” The people said, “Yes.” So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up and prayed two more rak‘ahs, then gave the greeting of peace. Then he pronounced the takbir and prostrated as he usually prostrated, or longer, then rose.

english_blocks: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed one of the two afternoon prayers—Muhammad said: I think it was most likely ‘Asr—as two rak‘ahs, then gave the greeting of peace.

Then he stood up and went to a piece of wood at the front of the mosque and placed his hand on it. Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, were among them, but they were too awed to speak to him. Those who were hurrying left and said, “Has the prayer been shortened?” A man whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called Dhu al-Yadayn said, “Did you forget, or has it been shortened?” He said, “I did not forget, and it has not been shortened.” He said, “Yes, you have forgotten.”

So he prayed two rak‘ahs, then gave the greeting of peace. Then he pronounced the takbir and prostrated as he usually prostrated, or longer. Then he raised his head and pronounced the takbir. Then he lowered his head and pronounced the takbir and prostrated as he usually prostrated, or longer. Then he raised his head and pronounced the takbir.

arabic_blocks: [1174] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة حدثنا هشام بن أبي عبد الله الدستوائي عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: إذا نودي بالصلاة أدبر الشيطان وله ضراط حتى لا يسمع الأذان فإذا قضي الأذان أقبل فإذا ثوب بها أدبر فإذا قضي التثويب أقبل حتى يخطر بين المرء ونفسه يقول اذكر كذا وكذا ما لم يكن يذكر حتى يظل الرجل إن يدري كم صلى فإذا لم يدر أحدكم كم صلى ثلاثا أو أربعا فليسجد سجدتين وهو جالس
english_blocks: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. Hisham ibn Abi ‘Abdullah al-Dastawa’i related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns away, passing wind so that he does not hear the adhan. When the adhan has ended, he comes back. When the iqamah is called for it, he turns away. When the iqamah has ended, he comes back, coming between a person and his own self, saying, “Remember such-and-such and such-and-such,” things he had not been remembering, until the man does not know how much he has prayed. If one of you does not know how much he has prayed, three or four, let him make two prostrations while seated.

arabic_blocks: [1176] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثني ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو عن بكير عن كريب ان ابن عباس والمسور بن مخرمة وعبد الرحمن بن أزهر رضى الله تعالى عنهم أرسلوه إلى عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فقالوا اقرأ عليها السلام منا جميعا وسلها عن الركعتين بعد صلاة العصر وقل لها إنا أخبرنا أنك تصلينهما وقد بلغنا أن النبي ﷺ نهى عنها، وقال ابن عباس وكنت أضرب الناس مع عمر بن الخطاب عنها، فقال كريب فدخلت على عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فبلغتها ما أرسلوني فقالت سل أم سلمة فخرجت إليهم فأخبرتهم بقولها فردوني إلى أم سلمة بمثل ما أرسلوني به إلى عائشة فقالت أم سلمة رضى الله تعالى عنها سمعت النبي ﷺ ينهى عنها ثم رأيته يصليهما حين صلى العصر ثم دخل وعندي نسوة من بني حرام من الأنصار فأرسلت إليه الجارية فقلت: قومي بجنبه قولي له تقول لك أم سلمة يا رسول الله سمعتك تنهى عن هاتين وأراك تصليهما فإن أشار بيده فاستأخري عنه ففعلت الجارية فأشار بيده فاستأخرت عنه فلما انصرف قال: يا بنت أبي أمية سألت عن الركعتين بعد العصر وإنه أتاني ناس من عبد القيس فشغلوني عن الركعتين اللتين بعد الظهر فهما هاتان
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: ‘Amr informed me, from Bukayr, from Kuraib:

Ibn ‘Abbas, al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Azhar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, sent him to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her. They said, “Convey greetings of peace to her from all of us. Ask her about the two rak‘ahs after the ‘Asr prayer, and say to her, ‘We have been informed that you pray them, but it has reached us that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade them.’” Ibn ‘Abbas said, “I used to strike people for them along with ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab.”

Kuraib said: I went in to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, and conveyed what they had sent me with. She said, “Ask Umm Salamah.” So I went out to them and told them what she had said. They sent me back to Umm Salamah with the same message they had sent me with to ‘A’ishah.

Umm Salamah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbid them. Then I saw him praying them when he had prayed ‘Asr. Then he entered, and I had with me women from Banu Haram of the Ansar. I sent the slave girl to him, saying, “Stand beside him. Say to him, ‘Umm Salamah says to you: O Messenger of Allah, I heard you forbid these two, and I see you praying them.’ If he signals with his hand, draw back from him.” The slave girl did so. He signalled with his hand, and she drew back from him.

When he finished, he said, “O daughter of Abu Umayyah, you asked about the two rak‘ahs after ‘Asr. Some people from ‘Abd al-Qays came to me and occupied me, keeping me from the two rak‘ahs after Dhuhr. These are those two.”

arabic_blocks: [1177] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد حدثنا يعقوب بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي حازم عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي رضى الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ بلغه أن بني عمرو بن عوف كان بينهم شيء فخرج رسول الله ﷺ يصلح بينهم في أناس معه فحبس رسول الله ﷺ وحانت الصلاة فجاء بلال إلى أبي بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه، فقال: يا أبا بكر إن رسول الله ﷺ قد حبس وقد حانت الصلاة فهل لك أن تؤم الناس قال: نعم إن شئت فأقام بلال وتقدم أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه فكبر للناس وجاء رسول الله ﷺ يمشي في الصفوف حتى قام في الصف فأخذ الناس في التصفيق وكان أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه لا يلتفت في صلاته فلما أكثر الناس التفت فإذا رسول الله ﷺ فأشار إليه رسول الله ﷺ يأمره أن يصلي فرفع أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه يديه فحمد الله ورجع القهقرى وراءه حتى قام في الصف فتقدم رسول الله ﷺ فصلى للناس فلما فرغ أقبل على الناس، فقال: يا أيها الناس ما لكم حين نابكم شيء في الصلاة أخذتم في التصفيق إنما التصفيق للنساء من نابه شيء في صلاته فليقل سبحان الله فإنه لا يسمعه أحد حين يقول سبحان الله إلا التفت يا أبا بكر ما منعك أن تصلي للناس حين أشرت إليك، فقال أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه ما كان ينبغي لابن أبي قحافة أن يصلي بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ
english_blocks: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. Ya‘qub ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

It reached the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that something had happened among Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out with some people to reconcile them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delayed, and the time for prayer came. Bilal came to Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, and said, “O Abu Bakr, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has been delayed, and the time for prayer has come. Would you lead the people?” He said, “Yes, if you wish.”

Bilal called the iqamah. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, went forward and pronounced the takbir for the people. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came walking through the rows until he stood in the row. The people began clapping. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, did not turn around during his prayer. When the people increased it, he turned, and there was the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, signalled to him, directing him to pray. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, raised his hands and praised Allah, then stepped backwards behind him until he stood in the row. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went forward and led the people in prayer.

When he finished, he turned towards the people and said, “O people, why, when something happened to you in prayer, did you begin clapping? Clapping is only for women. Whoever has something happen to him in his prayer should say, ‘Glory be to Allah,’ for no one hears him when he says ‘Glory be to Allah’ without turning around. O Abu Bakr, what prevented you from leading the people in prayer when I signalled to you?”
Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said, “It was not fitting for the son of Abu Quhafah to pray in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
